title: Backpressure hysteresis sampler — warmup and pressure runs (scratchpad)
content:
Purpose:
Run a focused set of pressure + warmup experiments to surface hysteresis in backpressure signals and autoscaler interactions. I suspected that the current cooldown window + hard queue watermark leads to oscillatory throughput/latency when we have short microbursts (50–250ms) at QPSs near capacity. This is a scratchpad log: notes, quick charts, and next experiments.

Environment / baseline:
- Model: open-7b-quant (int8 sim) pinned to runtime-2026-01 kernel set
- Hardware: synthetic cluster of 4x A100-80GB (shared pool), single allocation per shard for the test
- Runtime flags: batching=enabled, batch_max_tokens=2048, batch_timeout_ms=12, kv_cache=true
- Ingress: grpc client sim (locally controlled) using Poisson spike generator
- Autoscaler/policy: cool_down_ms=30000 (30s), queue_watermark=0.68 (68% of capacity), allow_burst=false
- Admission control: hard reject when queue length > N (N tuned per run)

Hypotheses:
1) With a fixed 30s cooldown, transient microbursts trigger scaling or backpressure, but the system does not re-allow full admission quickly enough, causing sawtooth throughput and repeated p99 spikes.
2) The hard watermark paired with immediate reject causes client retries that amplify arrival clustering (retry storm).
3) Shorten cooldown or change to a moving-average occupancy will reduce oscillation.

Experiment matrix (short):
- Run A: baseline traffic 120 qps steady for 2m, then 3 spikes of 5s at +200 qps spaced 15s apart. (control)
- Run B: same as A but cool_down_ms=10000 (10s)
- Run C: same as A but queue_watermark=0.85 and allow_burst=true (soft admission via token bucket)
- Run D: vary batch_timeout_ms from 6ms -> 24ms in steps while repeating A pattern

Key signals captured (sampling at 1s):
- p50/p95/p99 server latency (ms)
- observed qps (accepted)
- queue length (requests waiting)
- GPU utilization (per-GPU)
- batch size distribution (mean/std)
- reject_count and retry_rate (est from clients)

Representative excerpt (Run A, 2025-11-09 14:05 local):
- steady 120 qps: p50=28ms, p95=110ms, p99=310ms, gpu_util=64%
- spike 1 (+200 qps for 5s): within spike: accepted qps jumps to 270 qps for 1s then backpressure kicks in, queue length climbs to 86, p99 jumps to 980ms, reject_count=18 in 5s window
- 6s after spike: accepted qps oscillates 170 -> 95 -> 150 over 12s, p99 cycles 420 -> 640 -> 390ms
- pattern repeated for spikes 2/3; overall tail is correlated with cooldown end times

ASCII time series (smoothed 1s windows) — accepted qps (A):
steady: 120 |~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
spike:  270 |~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
after:  95  |~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Latency p99 snapshot (ms) across the spike window (A):
[t=0s] 310  [t=1s] 980  [t=2s] 620  [t=5s] 410  [t=12s] 640

Observations / quick conclusions from runs A vs B vs C:
- Shortening cooldown to 10s (Run B) reduced the duration of the oscillation after each spike: the system readmitted traffic faster and p99 drop was faster. However, it caused an extra brief transient where batch sizes shrank (smaller batches -> slightly higher p50) because the admission opened earlier than backend warmup (kv cache priming).
- Raising the watermark and allowing soft bursts (Run C) substantially reduced immediate rejects and client retry amplification. Tail latency decreased by ~25% at p99 compared to A, while avg GPU util rose by ~8%. This suggests token-bucket style soft admission is useful for microbursts.
- Increasing batch_timeout (Run D) to 24ms increased mean batch size which lowered p50 by ~6ms but increased p95 slightly during spikes because the queueing delay added to tail for some requests. There is a tradeoff between batching efficiency and added queue latency under bursty arrivals.

Root causes identified (working list):
- Autoscaler cooldown mismatch with kv-cache warmup: we open admission earlier but model execution still pays warmup penalty -> spike in token latency for some requests.
- Hard rejects amplify client-side retries; retries cluster and create secondary spikes.
- Batch timeout too small to capture sufficient batching during transients; too large adds queueing penalty.

Immediate remediation ideas (to proto):
- Implement moving-average occupancy for admission rather than simple watermark threshold (short window ~3s + long window ~20s) to smooth decisions.
- Add a soft-admit token bucket overlay: allow small over-provisioning for short windows instead of outright rejects.
- Tie admission re-open to a warming metric (e.g., kv-cache-hit-rate or per-token exec-latency trending down) so we only fully re-open after backend warmed.
- Add jittered retry backoff guidance to client SDK (avoid synchronized retries).

Priority next experiments (ordered):
1) Soft-admit token bucket (burst allowance 15%) + existing watermark. Re-run A pattern, measure reject_count and retry amplification.
2) Moving-average occupancy admission: implement quick inline in test harness; compare to hard watermark.
3) Autoscaler cooldown = adaptive: shorten cooldown when cluster GPU util remains high vs low. Test with cluster-level util gating.
4) Measure kv-cache priming time: instrument exec latency while warming with synthetic prefixes to get a quantifiable warmup time per model variant.

Notes to follow-up in code/infra:
- Add short metric: "admission_reopen_latency" (time between earliest admission-open signal and observed p50 improvement) to help tie warmup to admission policy.
- Consider exposing soft_admit configuration in Dedicated UI as an option for burst-friendly deployments.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Exact client retry behavior in production varies — are we seeing additional amplification due to gateway/proxy retries? Need logs from frontends.
- How do multi-tenant noisy neighbors affect watermark thresholds? Current tests are single-tenant. Need a multi-tenant sweep.

TODO (actionable):
- [ ] Implement token-bucket soft admit in the test harness (Lumi)
- [ ] Add admission_reopen_latency metric to runtime (Rajat)
- [ ] Run multi-tenant synthetic test with background 60% load + same spike pattern (Ava)
- [ ] Draft short proposal for adaptive cooldown strategy and link to INF-8342 (Lumi)

Quick TL;DR for slack share:  "Microbursts are triggering an oscillation because we pair a hard watermark with a long cooldown; soft admission + shorter/adaptive cooldown reduces p99 and avoids retry amplification. Next: token-bucket soft-admit + moving-average occupancy sweep."

Scratchpad end — saving raw logs to linked artifacts. Will iterate after token-bucket experiment.
